defects.view: Strikes tab: Strike map and Signed contracts by strike (GET /api/flows/flowlab/name?view=strikes)
defects.symptom: QQQ and AAPL answer 502 {code: chain_upstream, message: 'Market data provider returned an error'} with no x-chain headers, at 16:15 and again at 16:19 TRT on 2026-10-28. Both modules print 'Unavailable. Reading the feed failed.' Errors are never cached, so every view spends another charged call. The AAPL 502 came back about 0.25 s after the previous response (x-server-now 1793193572836, then 1793193573091), so the failure is fast and repeatable.
defects.rootCause: Two layers. (1) Certain: the route hides the cause. whyOf (server/flowlab.js:23-31) files as 'failed' every error that is not chain_timeout, a 429, a 404 or a 401/402/403/422. HARD_FAILURES.failed (:17-21) then rebuilds it as HttpError.of('chain_upstream') with the table's default message, which drops the original code, status and message. Run against each uwFetch error class, buildNameView gives the same 502 body for six causes: chain_too_large, a 5xx, a 4xx outside 401/402/403/404/422/429, an unparsable body, a network failure and chain_unconfigured. A timeout gives 504, a 401/402/403/422 gives 200 why=plan and a 404 gives 200 why=empty. The production answer therefore rules out a timeout, a rate limit, a 404 and a plan or entitlement refusal, so the 'entitlement unanswered' note (docs/vendor-coverage.md:51) is not the cause. Every other read in the same session worked, which rules out chain_unconfigured, and the same failure on two tickers four minutes apart makes a passing network fault unlikely. (2) Most likely class: chain_too_large. The op returns one row per strike per minute, 'not aggregated with each other'. A row with the observed flow-per-strike key set is about 584 bytes, so MAX_BYTES 524288 holds about 897 rows: fewer than 2.3 active strikes a minute over a 390-minute session. At 10 strikes a minute the body is 2.2 MiB, at 100 it is 21.7 MiB, and QQQ and AAPL trade far more strikes than that. The fast failure fits uwFetch's Content-Length precheck (worker.js:2194-2197), which cancels at the headers. No request of this op reads less. Its only other parameter, filter (NetPremium by default, Volume, Trades; 'Retrieve the strikes with the highest filter parameter'), picks which strikes rank and states no count and no time bound. The op was never observed on the wire (it is absent from scripts/flows-probe-shapes.json), and the fixture holds 351 rows at 10-minute steps (tests/gen-flowlab-fixtures.py:320-333), so no test ever met the real size.

Reproductions in <scratchpad>/flowlab-diag-calc/ (each takes a checkout root as its argument): mask.mjs maps nine error classes to the route's output (six give the identical 502); rows.mjs measures 584 B per minute row and 897 rows per 512 KiB.
defects.fix: Decided: read the daily /api/stock/{ticker}/flow-per-strike with {date: session} for both Strikes modules, and take the intraday op off the page. Reason: it is the only documented request that reads less, one row per strike for the session (est. 90 to 490 KiB for the busiest ETFs at 624 B a row). Its wire shape is observed, the nightly flow leg already reads it every night (scripts/flows-legs/flow.mjs:320), and it cannot fail for size. In the registry, flow-per-strike gains limiter 'ondemand', a member klass, maxBytes 1048576 and its read list. A new reducer: rows of another date answer not-session and name the date the feed sent; rows without a numeric strike are dropped and counted; a null side volume is withheld as a dash, never read as 0; the 24 strikes nearest spot are kept (card spot, else the busiest strike, as today). The rail shows (call ask - call bid) - (put ask - put bid) contracts per strike. The main module becomes a strike-by-side map of call ask, call bid, put ask and put bid contracts, with the sided share as coverage and no unsided column. NOT_BUILT gains 'Quarter-hour strike map not built: per-minute strike rows run too large.' The quarter-hour axis returns only if the probe measures a QQQ intraday body that a streamed row reducer can take under 16 MiB. Make the cap safe for memory: uwFetch counts bytes while it reads (the readBounded pattern in server/http.js) and cancels at the cap, instead of buffering a chunked body in full before measuring it (worker.js:2200-2205). Name the class: whyOf maps chain_too_large to 'cap' (already in REASONS), and the route answers chain_too_large with the read object described under instrumentation. A failure copy with its class is kept 60 s during the session and 300 s outside it, so a deterministic failure stops costing a token on every view.

The copy is one Cache API entry per ticker and session day (internalKey('flowlab', 'n/<T>/strikes/<day>')), shared by every member, with a TTL of 60 s during the session and 300 s outside it. It sits behind vendorGate (one MEMBER_VENDOR check) and takes one UW_ONDEMAND token through chargedFetch. Today every view spends 1 call and gets a 502, because errors are never cached.

defects.symptom: 200 with 50 rows, each {e, every figure null}: 39 rows on 2026-10-28, 5 on 10-29, 3 on 10-30 and 3 on 11-20, with 0 dropped. Sorted by expiry, the module lists 'Oct 28' twelve times, then '+38 more expiries in Details', and every Net cell draws the flat sign glyph beside the em dash. Greek flow read 2026-10-28 only by accident: chooseExpiry kept the first row because every size was null.
defects.rootCause: The page reads the wrong operation. flow-recent returns 'the latest flows for the given ticker', filtered by side (ALL/ASK/BID/MID) and min_premium ('The minimum premium requested trades should have'). That is the wording and the filters of option-contract/{id}/flow, which returns 'the last 50 option trades' as Option Trade rows. The spec's response reference for flow-recent, 'Flow per expiry', is a copy error, and the registry read list, the fixture generator (build_recent) and reduceRecent all followed it. One row is one option print: an Option Trade with expiry, executed_at, option_type, strike, price, size, premium, nbbo_bid, nbbo_ask and tags. It is not a per-expiry aggregate. An aggregate has exactly one row per expiry, while this body repeats 2026-10-28 39 times across 4 expiries; 50 rows is the default page; and the spread (mostly the next day's expiry, a few the following days and the monthly) is what the last prints of 2026-10-27 look like once the 10-27 series stopped at 16:00. The op has no date parameter, so it always returns the latest prints. reduceRecent (shared/flows-flowlab.js:668-695) requires only a day-string expiry and turns every absent field into null without failing (:679-681), so 50 prints became 50 all-null rows instead of 'unshaped'. Reproduced: reduceRecent on 50 Option Trade rows taken from the spec's example (invented ticker) returns the production row byte for byte. One more consequence: the strict scheduled probe will fail on flow-recent, because 13 of its 14 declared reads will not arrive.

'failed' excludes a plan refusal (401/402/403/422 read 'plan'), a 404 ('empty') and a timeout ('timeout'), so the unanswered entitlement in docs/vendor-coverage.md:89 is not the cause. Most likely class: too large. A 5xx (the spec documents a text/plain 500) or an unparsable body remain possible. Reason: it is documented as rounded price buckets of off-exchange and lit volume, so it is small. Its wire shape is observed, the registry already has it at limiter 'ondemand' with maxBytes 131072, and both the dossier and the nightly flow leg already read it. defects.fix: Decided, view by view. Nightly: callCeiling stops subtracting the extras spend. The stage gets its own 40-call allowance, and only the run's deadline stops it. Reason: the recorded plan's day line is 100M, the binding limits are the minute pace and the 90-minute deadline, and 31 calls take about 4 s at the nightly pace. After the close the stored keys then pre-warm the closed session. Route: nightly?k=corr answers {status: 'off'} at once while analytics is off. For groups and venues: when the market is closed, read the stored key and serve it if its session is the clock's day. Otherwise (market open, or no key for that session), build on demand through serveCachedVendorRead with cacheKey internalKey('flowlab', 'od/<k>/<day>'), gate vendorGate(env, session) and chargedFetch. Move the nightly sections into a builder under shared/ so the Worker and the nightly write the same payload. TTL: 300 s until an hour after the close, then 21,600 s (the session's figures are final); during the session, 300 s for groups and 120 s for venues. Add a per-isolate single flight keyed by the cache key inside serveCachedVendorRead (a Map inside createState), so members who arrive together share one 25-call build. While a view fills it keeps its skeleton and says 'Reading the feed.' (Groups: 'Reading the 25 flow groups from the feed.'). A nightly copy is stamped with its session, an on-demand copy with its read time in TRT. If a build fails and a stored copy of an earlier session exists, that copy is shown with 'From the <date> session.' instead of an error. Relations stays off, for the switch's own reason: the analytics payload is an undocumented nullable object, and the nightly sends range '3M' and calculations 'correlation', neither of them in the documented forms ('2month', 'full' or an ISO date; upper-case names). otherViews.note: The read itself is correct in production. Its fields match the observed screener shape (option_symbol, premium str#, volume and the eight side and class volumes num, strike str#, stock_price, last_fill, next_earnings_date). Limit 250 is the documented maximum, order premium and volume_oi_ratio are in the enum, every preset filter is a documented parameter, the date is the last session when the market is closed, and 250 rows at about 1.5 KB come to about 375 KB, under 512 KiB. The defect is in the lean. askBounds (shared/flows-flowlab.js:158-177) leaves mid_volume out of the buy side of both bounds (hi = (ask + none) / vol), and leanOf says Down when ask + none is under half. The site's own rule, leanRead in shared/flows-sides.js:161-177, treats between-the-quotes as side unknown (hi = (T - B) / T) and calls sellers only when 2B > T. Production shows 'QQQ Oct 27 720 Call 49-50% Down' (askLo 0.49981, stated 0.99996 of 339,738 contracts); by the site's rule that is Down only if fewer than 50 contracts traded at the mid. Fix: hi = (ask + mid + none) / vol, and Down only when 2 x bid > vol. Hold it with mid-heavy rows and a planted build of the old bound.

Fields match the spec (Option Trade, Option Contract Minute Ticks, Option Contract Price Level Volume), the bodies fit (limit 100 is about 150 KB, at most 405 minute rows about 200 KB, the profile is small), and the date is the last session when the market is closed. Three defects. (1) The drill's part() (assets/js/flows-drill.js:97) knows only empty, plan and an 'unreachable' the server never sends, so a part the server marks failed, timeout or limited (server/flowlab.js:83) reads 'The feed's answer had an unexpected shape'. (2) A core with one failed part is cached as a success, for 86,400 s when d is a past day (server/routes/flows-flowlab.js:82, ttlFor), which pins a transient failure for a day. (3) The three calls run one after another, up to 24 s at the 8 s deadline. Fix: map the server's reasons and the instrumentation classes one to one, keep a partial core for 60 s, and run the three reads together.

The trade fields match the spec's Flow Alert Detail (executed_at, size, price, premium, nbbo_bid, nbbo_ask, exchange). There is no parameter beyond the id, and the body is bounded by the route's 512 KiB cap (the registry says 128 KiB). The alert object in the spec's example carries rule_id, not alert_rule, so reduceAlert's rule (shared/flows-flowlab.js:576) may be null and the heading falls back to 'Alert'. The probe should record the detail's alert keys.

The parameters are valid: ticker_symbol, limit 100 (max 500), and newer_than and older_than at Eastern midnights, exactly the documented 24-hour limit. diagnose.instrumentation: Make every failed read name its class in a form that is safe to show. (1) uwFetchUnmetered (worker.js:2166-2215) attaches cause {kind, status, bytes, cap, ms} to every error it throws. kind is one of: network (fetch rejected), timeout (signal aborted), limited (429), status (any other non-OK answer; status set), too_large (declared or counted bytes past the cap; bytes set), unparsable (JSON.parse failed; bytes set), unconfigured. Bytes are counted while reading (the readBounded pattern), so the cap also bounds memory. (2) Flow Lab's read() keeps {op, class, status, bytes, cap, ms}. class is one of too_large, status_5xx, status_4xx, unparsable, timeout, network, limited, plan (401/402/403 only), empty (404), unconfigured. A 422 becomes status_4xx with status 422, because the spec documents 422 as 'Unprocessable Entity' on every operation and a parameter fault must not read as a plan limit. (3) A hard failure answers its own code (chain_too_large, chain_timeout, chain_rate_limited, else chain_upstream) with details {read: {...}}, which apiError already merges into the body, for example {error:{code:'chain_too_large',message:'Market data provider body is over the parse ceiling'}, read:{op:'strike-flow-intraday', class:'too_large', status:null, bytes:2283112, cap:524288, ms:184}}. A soft failure keeps why and adds the same object: read for one-read views, x.reads.<half> for levels, x.<part>.read for the contract core. The object is a fixed allowlist of the registry id, an enum and integers; it never carries a URL, query, header, key or body text. (4) The page and the drill print one sentence per class, each 14 words or fewer and clean under copy-lint: 'The feed's answer was larger than this page reads.', 'The feed answered with an error, status 503.', 'The feed refused this request, status 400.', 'The feed's answer was not readable data.', 'The feed was not reachable.', plus the existing timeout and limit sentences. The drill uses the same table, which fixes its mapping of failed to 'unshaped'. (5) The Worker logs logFailure('warn', 'flowlab read failed', {op, class, status, bytes, cap}) once per isolate per op and class every 10 minutes. The call meter records too_large as 'size' and unparsable as 'parse' instead of 'network' (worker.js:2157-2160), so /api/flows/coverage with FLOWS_METER on lists failure codes per op. A failure copy with its class is kept 60 s during the session and 300 s outside it, so repeated views neither spend tokens nor lose the reason. (6) Tests: a Worker stub fetch per class (Content-Length past the cap, a chunked body past the cap, 503 text/plain, 400 JSON, 200 with invalid JSON, a rejected fetch, an abort) asserts the code, class, status and bytes, and scans the body for the URL and the key. Planted builds: chain_too_large filed as failed; details dropped when the error is rebuilt; a url key added to read; the meter recording size as network; a failure copy kept for the success TTL. (7) Settling the class for the two retired reads needs no member read. The strict scheduled probe (flows-probe.yml, Sundays at 17:23 TRT, AAPL and NVDA by default) already lists flow-per-strike-intraday and stock-volume-price-levels at tier used and records status, bytes and parse for each. A dispatch with the filter 'flow-per-strike-intraday,stock-volume-price-levels,flow-recent' and the tickers QQQ,AAPL gives the same result at once, and it will also show flow-recent's 13 unseen reads. Until the ceiling fix ships, tonight's meta stage detail {flCalls: 0, flSkipped: 4} confirms D4(b). The worktree has been removed. The reproduction scripts (mask.mjs, recent.mjs, cap.mjs, rows.mjs, census.mjs; each takes a checkout root as its argument) are in <scratchpad>/flowlab-diag-calc/.

items.alternative: The root cause holds, and our own evidence upgrades it from inferred to measured. Two of the supporting claims are wrong, though. Since 906d655 (2026-10-17) the scheduled flows-probe has asked this op as a tier-2 entitlement row. Run 39149470245 (job 117739964235, Sunday 2026-10-18 20:24 TRT, session 2026-10-16) and run 40217600578 (job 121242029772, Sunday 2026-10-25 20:40 TRT, session 2026-10-23) both answered 200. AAPL: 1.17 MB (2,555 rows) and 670.7 KB (1,427 rows). NVDA: 1.34 MB (2,850 rows) and 1.51 MB (3,238 rows). Each body arrived in 145-248 ms with envelope {data:[...]} and 21 keys. Those keys are timestamp, date, ticker, strike (decimal string), the four side volumes, call and put volume, the six premiums, call and put trades, and three undocumented fields (trades, volume, net_premium). There are no otm fields. Every body is 1.31x to 3.02x the 524,288-byte cap, so the path is chain_too_large, then whyOf 'failed', then 502 chain_upstream. That is confirmed for AAPL, and the plan, 404 and 5xx branches are excluded for it; I reran mask.mjs and cap.mjs on dfe0cad and got the same mapping. What is refuted: (1) 'never observed on the wire' is false: it was observed twice, but tier-2 answers are printed in the run log and never written to scripts/flows-probe-shapes.json. (2) The size model is wrong (every active strike every minute, 584 B a row, 2.2 MiB at 10 strikes and 21.7 MiB at 100). The wire row is 480-493 B and the op returns only 1.4K-3.2K rows a session. That fits its filter parameter ('strikes with the highest filter parameter'), not every active strike. (3) The 0.25 s failure does not point to the Content-Length precheck: the probe downloaded and parsed the whole body in 145-248 ms, so either path fits. QQQ is the one name still unmeasured. A flows-probe workflow_dispatch with tickers QQQ,SPY and filter flow-per-strike-intraday,stock-volume-price-levels,flow-recent,flow-per-expiry,flow-per-strike,darkpool-levels separates its case without a member read or a code change. The log prints status, bytes, rows, envelope and key types, never values. A 200 over 524,288 bytes means too_large, a non-2xx status means 4xx or 5xx, and 'not JSON' means unparsable.
items.betterFix: Do not take the intraday op off the page. The diagnosis retires it because 'per-minute strike rows run too large' and keeps the quarter-hour axis only below 16 MiB, but the measured bodies are 0.65-1.51 MB, so both premises fail. Decided: the route uses a per-op cap, opById(id).maxBytes, falling back to MAX_BYTES. strike-flow-intraday gets maxBytes 4,194,304, which is 2.7x the largest measured body (NVDA 1.51 MB on 2026-10-23); AAPL's expiration-Friday body was 1.75x its ordinary-day body. Keep the diagnosis's bounded read in uwFetch (count bytes, cancel at the cap) and its whyOf 'cap' class with the read object. Cache only the reduced map (24 strikes by 26 buckets, a few KB). On chain_too_large the view makes one fallback read of the daily flow-per-strike for the rail and says the quarter-hour map was over the size this page reads; that failure copy is kept 60 s in the session and 300 s outside it. items.alternative: Not refuted. The body alone rules out per-expiry aggregates, whatever the rows really are: 39 of 50 rows share one expiry, and all 12 figure fields are absent or null in every row. reduceRecent keeps a row only when each field that is present parses, so a malformed value would have dropped the row, not left it null. (1) Use the observed shape: a bare array of 23 rows (AAPL) or 25 (NVDA), 13.4-14.7 KB, 23 keys with a date string on every row and no top-level date, so the reducer reads row.date. items.betterFix:
Keep the daily flow-per-strike read with {date: session}, with these changes:
(1) Read it with the session-date reader the ticker page already uses for the same operation and day. Export sessionDated and netPremiumOf from shared/flows-positioning.js:538-550 (flowStrike builds card-x's net by strike from them) and import them into shared/flows-flowlab.js, so the two pages cannot disagree.
(2) The rail: show net premium by strike by the site's convention, (call ask - call bid) - (put ask - put bid) in exact cents. Print it as an interval, net ± unsided, where unsided = call_premium - call ask - call bid + put_premium - put ask - put bid, with the sided share beside it. Draw a direction mark only when the printed interval excludes zero (netProof in shared/flows-sfc-display.js); otherwise draw a hollow mark. A bare (ca-cb)-(pa-pb) is a point lean, which the owner's rule forbids. The map shows the four sided contract counts per strike with the sided share and no unsided column.
(3) Drop `spot` from the name-view cache key (server/routes/flows-flowlab.js:110). The page never sends it, so any client value only forks a copy and spends a call. Centre the 24 rows on the busiest strike on the server.

In the same change raise greek-flow-expiry and group-greek-flow-expiry from 131072 to 524288, or wiring the caps breaks the Greek flow that works today (QQQ about 165 KB).
(5) Count bytes while reading and decode once (agree with the diagnosis).
(6) Failures: never write a failure copy under the success key. serveCachedVendorRead keeps the last good copy for 6 h (VENDOR_COPY_KEEP_SECONDS) to answer refusals, and a failure written over it destroys that copy. Instead, write a sibling negative mark (internalKey('flowlab-fail', key), following the dossier's markUrl/MARK_TTL_S pattern):
- 60 s for 5xx, network and timeout;
- until clock.day changes for too_large and 4xx, since an intraday body only grows.
On a fresh hard failure with a kept good copy, serve that copy stamped X-Fresh-State: stale with the class, not a 502.
(7) TTL: ttlFor uses 300 s whenever the market is closed, although option figures are final an hour after the close. Give the option views 21,600 s from 17:00 ET and the stock views (lit prints, off-exchange levels) 21,600 s from 20:00 ET.
(8) Return flow-per-strike-intraday and stock-volume-price-levels to probe tier 2 and the entitlement list, as they were before #283, so Sunday keeps recording status and bytes. If the quarter-hour axis ever returns, cache it once per ticker per quarter hour, not per minute.

The single flight. A Worker cannot share a Response across requests, so the flight must hold the built payload inside serveCachedVendorRead rather than wrap the call. A promise whose fetches belong to another request can also be cancelled, or never settle, once that request ends. That is why the repository's cross-request flights (the market snapshot and schema bootstrap in worker.js:514-544, the clock in shared/flows-live-worker.js:142-185) join with settledWithin: a bounded wait, then abandon, retry and log flightAbandoned. The foreground build. 25 calls, five at a time, under the 8 s Flow Lab deadline can hold one request for up to about 40 s. The repository's fan-out pattern for many sources is the dossier's: a 3 s foreground wait, the rest in ctx.waitUntil, unfinished parts shown as pending and picked up on the next read.
